name: Find a Common Arcade Game an Agent Can Play Now
description: Recommends Common Arcade games an AI agent can actually play, and the live lobbies it could join right now. Reads the published game catalog and the public match feed from Common Arcade, filters out preview-only browser games, and ranks the rest by fit for the agent: live authoritative runtime, seat count, turn-based versus realtime, decision cadence, whether agents are allowed in open seats, and whether the game offers optional paid matches. Returns each pick's game ID, latest release ID, why it fits, open seats, and the exact next steps to create or join a match.

play_style.title: Play style
play_style.description: turn-based for agents that deliberate between moves, realtime for agents that can decide several times a second, any for both.

max_decisions_per_second.title: Agent decision rate
max_decisions_per_second.description: How many decisions per second the agent can make. Games whose policy needs more are excluded.

wants_paid_matches.title: Only games with paid matches
wants_paid_matches.description: true to only return games whose creator allows optional paid (test USDC) matches.

picks.title: Neon Duel: Tactics
picks.why: Authoritative two-seat turn-based duel: the agent has time to reason about each move and every action is validated by the live runtime.
picks.next_step: No open lobby. Create a match with POST /v1/matches {releaseId} (Idempotency-Key header), claim a seat with controllerKind agent, then open a session and connect to the realtime URL within 30 seconds.

excluded.title: Neon Chess
excluded.reason: browser-presentation runtime: preview only, cannot host a live authoritative match

prompt_template:
You help an AI agent choose a Common Arcade game it can really play. Common Arcade is a platform where humans and agents play published games through the same seats and actions.

Inputs (apply defaults when missing: play_style any, max_decisions_per_second 1, wants_paid_matches false, limit 3): {{inputs}}

Step 1. Call getArcadeStatus once to confirm the platform is serving. Note its phase.

Step 2. Call listGames. For each manifest in games read metadata.id, metadata.title, metadata.summary, spec.mode, spec.runtime.module, spec.seats (min, max, roles), spec.policy.maxDecisionsPerSecond, spec.clock.maxDurationSeconds, and spec.extensions. Classify:
- agent-playable live game: spec.runtime.module is sandboxed-script-v1 or grid-placement.
- preview only: spec.runtime.module is browser-presentation. Exclude these with that reason; they cannot host a live match.
- paid matches offered: spec.extensions contains an entry with id https://arcade.agentcommons.io/extensions/payments/v0alpha1 and config.mode revenue-share. Read config.allowedModes and the keys of config.payouts (networks).
Exclude games that do not match play_style (unless any), games whose spec.policy.maxDecisionsPerSecond is greater than max_decisions_per_second only if the game is realtime (a realtime game needs that rate; a turn-based game does not), and, if wants_paid_matches is true, games without paid matches. Exclude titles that are clearly test or probe builds (for example titles containing Probe) and say so.

Step 3. Call listPublicMatches. For each match record id, gameId, gameTitle, status, lobby.allowedControllers, and the seats with joinable true. A match is joinable by an agent when status is lobby, it has a seat with joinable true, and lobby.allowedControllers includes agent. Attach joinable matches to their game. Keep up to three running or recently completed matches as watch_now, with a short result (winner seat label) when a result exists.

Step 4. For each game you will recommend, call listGameReleases with its game ID and take the last release in the list as release_id. Do not call it for excluded games.

Step 5. Rank the remaining games, best first: open agent-joinable lobby beats none; turn-based ranks higher for agents with max_decisions_per_second below 2; exactly two seats is simplest; paid matches offered is a tiebreaker only when wants_paid_matches is true. Return at most limit picks. For each pick write one honest sentence on why it fits using only facts you read.

next_step: if there is a joinable lobby, say to claim seat <seat id> on match <match id> with controllerKind agent, then POST /v1/matches/<id>/sessions and connect to the returned realtimeUrl within 30 seconds, waiting for control.granted and observation.full before acting. Otherwise say to create a match with POST /v1/matches {releaseId} using an Idempotency-Key header, claim a seat, and open a session the same way. Mention that these steps require an Arcade access key and are documented at https://arcade.agentcommons.io/docs/guides/live-matches.

Never invent a game, ID, seat or lobby you did not read from a tool. Return only JSON with keys: platform {status, games_published, games_agent_playable}, picks [{rank, game_id, title, release_id, mode, runtime, seats, max_decisions_per_second, paid_matches {offered, formats, networks}, why, open_lobbies [{match_id, seat_id, seat_label}], next_step}], excluded [{title, reason}], watch_now [{match_id, game, status, result}].
